_comment: Seed source catalogue for the newsdesk. Probe figures (last_seen, per_week)
were measured on 2026-08-19 by fetching and parsing every feed — they are
observations, not estimates, and they go stale. The fetcher re-measures.
tier:  core     read nearly everything, low volume, high hit-rate
watch    good source, moderate volume, judge trims
firehose high volume, hard cap, discovery surface only
cap:   maximum items this source may put on the shortlist per edition.
Caps are the whole reason a 2/wk newsletter is not buried by a

dormant: this source had published nothing for over 120 days when the catalogue was built. It is kept deliberately — polling costs nothing and the point is to notice if it WAKES UP. Dormant sources are excluded from the edition's stale-source warnings (a warning that fires every single day is one you stop reading), and the flag clears itself the moment the source publishes again, which is announced once.

note: ALSO an editorial instruction. The reader is handed each candidate's note as `source_note` and told to obey it, so a source's standing policy ('discussion only, never build logs') is DATA that can be retuned here without touching the judge prompt.

sources.name: Bitcoin Optech Newsletter
sources.note: The single highest-signal Bitcoin source in existence. Weekly, technical, zero price talk.

sources.name: Delving Bitcoin (forum)
sources.note: Where protocol arguments actually happen, before they reach any podcast.

sources.name: Bitcoin Core PR Review Club
sources.note: Runs in seasons; long gaps are normal, not a dead feed.

sources.name: 0xB10C
sources.note: Mempool/network measurement from someone who instruments the real thing.

sources.name: Brink (bitcoin dev funding)
sources.note: Who is being paid to work on what — a leading indicator of what lands next year.

sources.name: Blockstream engineering
sources.note: Engineering posts are good; marketing posts are not. Judge filters.

sources.name: Jameson Lopp
sources.note: Self-custody and node operations, occasionally security-research grade.

sources.name: Stacker News (top)
sources.note: Community aggregator. Capped hard; it is a discovery surface, not a source. EDITORIAL: aggregator. Publish only if the discussion itself is the value.

sources.name: Fedimint blog
sources.note: DORMANT since 2025-06. Kept because it is cheap and would matter if it revives.

sources.name: Bitcoin Knots releases
sources.note: He runs Knots.

sources.name: Forgejo releases
sources.note: He self-hosts it and it is the source of truth for every repo.

sources.name: Lyn Alden
sources.note: Rare, long, structural. Publishes ~monthly; every piece is worth the slot.

sources.name: Bank Underground (BoE staff)
sources.note: Bank of England staff writing without a press office. Genuinely esoteric.

sources.name: Liberty Street Economics (NY Fed)
sources.note: Same idea from the NY Fed: primary research, no punditry layer.

sources.name: FRED Blog
sources.note: Short, data-first, one chart per post.

sources.name: Adam Tooze — Chartbook
sources.note: Economic history applied to the present. Verbose; the judge trims.

sources.name: Wolf Street
sources.note: Credit, housing, freight. Reads the data series, not the narrative.

sources.name: Klement on Investing
sources.note: One research note a day, usually a paper summarised honestly.

sources.name: Conversable Economist
sources.note: Timothy Taylor surfacing working papers most people never see.

sources.name: Doomberg
sources.note: Energy-first macro. PAYWALLED — expect headline + teaser only.

sources.name: Apricitas Economics
sources.note: Chart-heavy. Quiet since May 2026.

sources.name: Marginal Revolution
sources.note: 35/wk of mostly links. Capped; occasionally the best thing all week.

sources.name: Mises Wire
sources.note: Heavy ideological load at 35/wk. Cap 1 and let the judge earn it.

sources.name: Low-tech Magazine
sources.note: The closest thing to a house journal for this interest. NOTE: expired TLS cert on their solar-powered server — needs an explicit per-feed insecure flag.

sources.name: Do the Math (Tom Murphy)
sources.note: A physicist doing the arithmetic on energy claims. Nearly zero noise.

sources.name: Drive On Wood forum
sources.note: His own wood-gas community. Forum firehose is small (1.2/wk) and on-topic by construction. EDITORIAL: publish only DISCUSSION — people arguing, diagnosing, or working a problem out. Chris knows what a gasifier is and does not need another build log. Reject photo threads, build pictures, show-and-tell and 'here is my rig' posts however on-topic they look.

sources.name: Wood gas: Gasifiers forum (Reddit)
sources.note: Tiny volume, perfectly on-topic. Nothing else covers gasification this directly. EDITORIAL: same as Drive On Wood — ideas and problem-solving only, never build logs or photo dumps.

sources.name: Construction Physics
sources.note: How things get built and why they cost what they cost.

sources.name: Practical Engineering
sources.note: Infrastructure explained by an engineer who builds it.

sources.name: Energy Institute at Haas
sources.note: Grid economics from people who model it.

sources.name: Hackaday: Green Hacks tag
sources.note: The Hackaday sub-feed that is actually on-topic, without the other 48/wk.

sources.name: Resilience.org
sources.note: Good material buried in advocacy. Cap and judge hard.

sources.name: Backwoods/Off-grid: Solar Power World
sources.note: Trade press. Mostly product announcements; occasionally a real install teardown.

sources.name: All Power Labs
sources.note: DORMANT since 2026-01. The commercial gasifier people; worth noticing if they wake.

sources.name: No Tech Magazine
sources.note: DORMANT since 2025-06. Sister publication to Low-tech.

sources.name: Open Source Ecology
sources.note: DORMANT since 2025-07.

sources.name: Living Energy Farm
sources.note: DORMANT since 2025-05. Off-grid DC power done for real, at a working farm.

sources.name: Front Porch Republic
sources.note: Localism, place, scale, limits. The intellectual end of simple living.

sources.name: Small Farmer's Journal
sources.note: Draft animals and small-farm practice. Nobody else publishes this.

sources.name: Dry Creek Chronicles (wordpress)
sources.note: Rick's blog. Quiet since 2024-11 — this is how he finds out if it restarts.

sources.name: The Prairie Homestead
sources.note: Practical homestead technique. Some course-selling; judge filters.

sources.name: Root Simple
sources.note: Urban homesteading, low-tech skills. Slow lately.

sources.name: Backwoods Home Magazine
sources.note: Nearly dormant (last post 2025-12), long archive of real technique.

sources.name: LWN.net headlines
sources.note: The kernel and distro record of account. Some items paywalled for a week.

sources.name: Rachel by the Bay
sources.note: Operational war stories, unmatched. WARNING: her server refused/timed out on both probe attempts from gromit — verify fetchability before trusting this slot. ⚠️ OBSERVED 2026-08-19/20: times out from gromit on every attempt. Kept because the writing is worth chasing down, but expect it to sit in the failing list until the cause is found.

sources.name: Julia Evans
sources.note: Explains the thing you thought you understood.

sources.name: Dan Luu
sources.note: Rare and long. Every post is a slot well spent.

sources.name: Self-Host Weekly (noted.lol)
sources.note: A human already did the self-hosting triage for the week.

sources.name: NixOS blog
sources.note: Release announcements and RFC outcomes.

sources.name: Michael Stapelberg
sources.note: Distri/Debian internals, home network engineering.

sources.name: Vermaden (BSD/UNIX ops)
sources.note: Deep UNIX ops write-ups, weekly-ish valuable link roundups.

sources.name: Xe Iaso
sources.note: NixOS-adjacent infrastructure writing.

sources.name: Drew DeVault
sources.note: Opinionated; occasionally an important systems argument.

sources.name: Jeff Geerling
sources.note: Homelab hardware tested by someone who publishes the failures.

sources.name: Determinate Systems blog
sources.note: Nix tooling from the people shipping most of it.

sources.name: Tailscale blog
sources.note: He runs it as the perimeter at home and at work.

sources.name: Servethehome
sources.note: Server hardware teardowns and used-gear economics.

sources.name: Krebs on Security
sources.note: The security story that actually matters, once or twice a week.

sources.name: r/selfhosted (top/week)
sources.note: Pre-ranked by the sub. Discovery of tools, not analysis. ⚠️ OBSERVED: Reddit rate-limits this box (HTTP 429) intermittently — succeeded on two of three real runs. EDITORIAL: a discovery surface. Publish a tool only if the post explains something about running it, not because it exists.

sources.name: NixOS Discourse
sources.note: 42/wk. Mine for breakage reports on modules he runs. EDITORIAL: reject ordinary support requests and one-person breakage. Publish design discussion, RFC outcomes, and breakage that affects modules he runs.

sources.name: lobste.rs
sources.note: 175/wk, high average quality. The judge earns its keep here. EDITORIAL: aggregator. Judge the linked thing, never the ranking.

sources.name: Hacker News (best)
sources.note: 210/wk even filtered to 'best'. Pure discovery surface. EDITORIAL: aggregator. Judge the linked thing, never the ranking.

sources.name: Phoronix
sources.note: 112/wk of benchmarks and kernel commits. Cap hard.

sources.name: Hackaday
sources.note: 49/wk. The general feed; Green Hacks is carried separately.

sources.name: oss-security (openwall)
sources.note: Filter to software he actually runs, else it is 35/wk of other people's CVEs.

sources.name: Ubuntu Security Notices
sources.note: Work-relevant: every Broadlinc backend VM is Ubuntu. Filter to installed packages.

sources.name: APNIC Blog
sources.note: Routing, DNS and measurement, written by operators.

sources.name: RIPE Labs
sources.note: Same, from the European registry. Esoteric and genuinely useful.

sources.name: Cloudflare Blog
sources.note: Post-mortems and protocol work; skip the product launches.

sources.name: Telecompetitor (rural broadband)
sources.note: 35/wk, press-release heavy — but it is the BEAD/rural-funding beat, which is his industry. ⚠️ OBSERVED: returns HTTP 403 to a scripted user-agent on every attempt. It will decay into dormancy rather than warn forever; needs a browser UA or dropping.

sources.name: Ars/Broadband? Light Reading
sources.note: Telecom trade press. Cap 1; mostly vendor noise.

sources.name: Simon Willison
sources.note: The most reliable LLM-practice signal available, 19/wk of it. EDITORIAL: he posts many short release notes. Publish the essays and the worked experiments; reject bare 'library 1.2.3 released' entries.

sources.name: Ken Shirriff
sources.note: Chip and hardware archaeology. Nothing else like it.

sources.name: Bunnie Huang
sources.note: Hardware, supply chains, manufacturing reality.

sources.name: Works in Progress
sources.note: Long-form on why progress stalls. Quarterly-ish.

sources.name: Astral Codex Ten
sources.note: Long and uneven. Cap 2 and let the judge be ruthless.

sources.name: fasterthanli.me
sources.note: Quiet since 2025-12. Deep systems explainers when it moves.

dropped.name: Bitcoin Magazine Technical
dropped.why: 70 items/wk, overwhelmingly price and personality. This is precisely the noise he asked to be spared.

dropped.name: Calculated Risk
dropped.why: THE BLOG ENDED. Final post 2026-01-21, titled 'This is the End and a New Beginning'. Would have looked alive from the feed's item count alone.

dropped.name: Proxmox VE roadmap/news
dropped.why: The forum id in that URL is not announcements — it returns general support threads ('Easiest way of migrating to new system disk?'). No usable announce-only feed found.

dropped.name: NANOG (mail-archive)
dropped.why: The mail-archive mirror stopped at 2025-03. A stale mirror that still returns 100 items is exactly the 'empty result has two causes' trap.

dropped.name: The Deliberate Agrarian
dropped.why: Last post 2020-07. Archive is worth reading; a feed is not worth polling.

dropped.name: Gwern
dropped.why: gwern.net/index.xml and /atom.xml both serve HTML, not a feed.

wanted_no_feed.name: bitcoin-dev mailing list
wanted_no_feed.why: gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/new.atom returns HTTP 418 to this user-agent. Worth one more attempt with a browser UA — this is a high-value source Optech only partly covers.

wanted_no_feed.name: Chaincode Labs
wanted_no_feed.why: chaincode.com has no feed; blog.chaincode.com does not resolve.

wanted_no_feed.name: Michael Pettis (China Financial Markets)
wanted_no_feed.why: Carnegie's RSS paths all 404 or return non-feed content.

wanted_no_feed.name: BIS publications
wanted_no_feed.why: Both documented .rss paths 404. BIS quarterly reviews would be a strong macro source if a path can be found.

wanted_no_feed.name: Benton Institute broadband headlines
wanted_no_feed.why: Returns non-feed content on every documented path. The best rural-broadband policy digest there is; worth a manual look for the real URL.

wanted_no_feed.name: MikroTik news
wanted_no_feed.why: No RSS found. He runs MikroTik everywhere; a changelog feed would be valuable. Fallback: poll the changelog page for diffs.

wanted_no_feed.name: Mother Earth News
wanted_no_feed.why: HTTP 500 on every feed path — server-side, may recover.

wanted_no_feed.name: Permaculture News
wanted_no_feed.why: Returns HTML, not XML, on /feed/ and /rss/.

wanted_no_feed.name: Practical Farmers of Iowa
wanted_no_feed.why: Feed parses but contains zero items.
